definition: The drawing of a sound's amplitude over time.
note: Audacity pl uses „kształt fali”, Ardour pl „wykres fali”. „Przebieg” (przebieg czasowy) is the electronics and studio word and combines well (przebieg szczytowy, przebieg rzeźbiony); write „przebieg fali” in docs where the context is unclear.

definition: A picture of how a sound's frequency content changes over time: time across, frequency up, level as colour.
note: Audacity pl and Ardour pl. „Sonogram” is an older variant, still common in bioacoustics.

definition: A frequency scale spaced as pitch is heard: roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.
note: Unit „mel”; Polish Wikipedia: „Mel (skala)”.

definition: The moving line that marks the current playback position.
note: Ardour pl: „głowica”; Audacity pl: „wskaźnik odtwarzania”. Do not call it „kursor” (that is the edit cursor). The app name Playhead stays in English.

definition: The position where editing and playback start, set by clicking.
note: Audacity pl: „Kursor”; Ardour pl: „punkt edycji” (edit point).

definition: Samples per second of a digital sound, in Hz.
note: Audacity, Ardour, LMMS pl; TVP technical requirements.

definition: Bits per sample of a digital sound; sets its resolution.
note: Audacity pl („Rozdzielczość bitowa”), Polish Wikipedia („Rozdzielczość bitowa dźwięku”), TVP („rozdzielczość … bitów/próbkę”). „Głębia bitowa” is a common calque. „Sets its resolution” is rendered as accuracy, to avoid „rozdzielczość… rozdzielczość”.

definition: One signal of a sound file; stereo has two.
One channel.
note: Indeclinable (ścieżka mono); adjective „monofoniczny” in formal text.

definition: Two channels, left and right.
note: Indeclinable; adjective „stereofoniczny”.

definition: Stereo written as the sum (mid) and the difference (side) of the channels.
note: Polish engineers say „M/S”, „technika M/S”, or „mid/side”; the descriptive „sygnał sumaryczny i różnicowy” is used in textbooks.

definition: Where in its cycle a wave is at a given moment.
Whether a signal is upright or inverted.
note: Audacity pl: „biegunowość”; Ardour pl and studio speech: „polaryzacja” (in electronics „polaryzacja” also means bias, so „biegunowość” is the cleaner term). Do not say „odwrócenie fazy” for a plain inversion.

definition: How strong a signal is, usually in dB.
note: Measured quantity. Do not use „głośność” for it, although everyday Polish calls the volume control „głośność”.

definition: A change of level, in dB.
note: Audacity, Ardour, LMMS pl. A negative value is still „wzmocnienie” (−6 dB). „Gain” is common in speech (gain staging).

definition: The largest absolute sample value.
note: Audacity pl („Szczyt”, „Poziom szczytowy”), TVP („miernik wartości szczytowej”).

definition: The peak of the signal between samples, as a DAC would reproduce it.
note: No settled Polish term. TVP delivery specs write „Maksymalny chwilowy poziom sygnału („True Peak”)” and Ardour pl keeps „True Peak”; unit dBTP. Use the loan in the UI and add the Polish gloss on first use in docs. DAC = przetwornik C/A.
alternatives: rzeczywisty poziom szczytowy; maksymalny chwilowy poziom sygnału

definition: How loud a sound is heard, as opposed to its level.
note: Psychoacoustic quantity (son, LUFS); KRRiT regulation Dz.U. 2013 poz. 48, Ardour pl („Analiza głośności”). Keep „poziom” for measured level. „Poziom głośności” in acoustics is loudness level in phons, while Polish broadcast rules use it for programme loudness in LUFS, so qualify it when you use it.

definition: Loudness units relative to full scale (ITU-R BS.1770); 1 LU is 1 dB.
note: KRRiT regulation (Dz.U. 2013 poz. 48): LU, „jednostka pomiarowa głośności”; LUFS, „jednostka głośności wyrażona w LU w odniesieniu do pełnej skali”.

definition: The frequency weighting that loudness meters apply before measuring.
note: Modelled on A-weighting in Polish noise standards („charakterystyka częstotliwościowa A”, „poziom dźwięku A”); „ważenie K” is the usual broadcast-engineering calque.

definition: Set a sound's peak or loudness to a target.
note: Glossary form is the verbal noun; the UI command is „Normalizuj” (Audacity, Ardour pl). Specify „normalizacja szczytowa” or „normalizacja głośności”.

definition: A gradual change of level at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out).
note: Generic „przejście” as in Audacity and Ardour pl („Typ przejścia”, „Długość przejścia”). For the two directions use „zgłośnienie” (fade-in) and „wyciszenie” (fade-out); Audacity has „Zgłośnienie”/„Ściszenie”. In speech, „fade-in/fade-out”.

definition: Distortion when a signal exceeds the largest value that can be stored.
note: Ardour pl and studio speech use „przesterowanie” (clip indicator); Audacity pl uses „obcinanie” („Znajdź obcinanie”, „miękkie obcinanie”). Use „obcinanie (clipping)” where it must be told apart from analogue overdrive or saturation.

definition: A constant shift of the signal away from zero.
note: Electronics term for the DC component; Audacity pl: „offset DC”.

definition: The level of the background noise under a sound.
note: Audacity pl: „Poziom szumu”. Equipment self-noise is „szumy własne”.

definition: A stretch with no sound above the noise floor.
A sound that ends before its decay has died away.
One recorded or rendered version of a sound.
note: Ardour pl keeps „take” (genitive „take'a”). Polish film and recording studios also say „dubel”, which declines easily (duble, dubli). For generated output, „wersja” is a neutral fallback.

definition: Compute a processed sound and write it as audio.
note: Audacity pl: „Renderuj”; Ardour pl uses „Zrzuć” for bounce. „Zgrać” is studio speech for writing a mix to a file.

definition: A sound that repeats without an audible join.
note: Audacity, Ardour, LMMS pl; verb „zapętlić”.

definition: A fade-out of one sound overlapping a fade-in of another.
note: Audacity pl: „Przenikanie”; Ardour pl: „przejście krzyżowe”; in speech, „crossfade”.

definition: Cut a sound into parts at chosen points.
note: Verbal noun as the glossary form; the UI command is „Potnij”. Call the parts „fragmenty” (sampler slang: „slice'y”). Audacity and Ardour pl use „Podziel” for split.

definition: Change a sound's duration without changing its pitch.
note: Ardour pl („rozciąganie w czasie”), Audacity pl („rozciągnięty w czasie”).

definition: Change a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
note: Audacity pl: „Zmień wysokość” (Change Pitch), „Przesunięcie wysokości” (Pitch Shift). „Transpozycja” is the musical term, for whole-semitone shifts.

definition: The unit of loudness as heard; 1 sone is the loudness of a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL.
note: Polish Wikipedia: „Son (głośność dźwięku)”; plural „sony”.

definition: How much a sound's energy sits at high frequencies, as heard; in acum.
note: Polish psychoacoustics (A. Preis, UAM Poznań, in naukawpolsce.pl). Studio speech also calls a harsh sound „ostry”, but in these apps „ostrość” is kept for DIN 45692 sharpness only; harshness is „nieprzyjemność”.

definition: The rasping quality of fast amplitude modulation (about 15–300 Hz); in asper.
note: A. Preis (naukawpolsce.pl) and M. Gałuszka (twojazielonka.org) use „chropowatość”; „szorstkość” is an equivalent variant also found in Polish texts. Keep both away from harshness („nieprzyjemność”).

definition: The sensation of slow amplitude modulation (about 1–20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz); in vacil.
note: A. Preis (naukawpolsce.pl), M. Gałuszka (twojazielonka.org).

definition: Zwicker's combination of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength into one annoyance value.
note: „Uciążliwość hałasu” is the established Polish noise-annoyance term in environmental acoustics; A. Preis uses „dokuczliwość”. Harshness („nieprzyjemność”) is derived from it but is a separate term.

definition: One sound making another harder or impossible to hear.
note: Standard in Polish psychoacoustics, audiology („maskowanie przesłuchu”, UAM) and perceptual coding. Polish Wikipedia titles the article „Zagłuszanie (akustyka)”, but audio usage is „maskowanie”.

definition: The frequency range the ear integrates as one; on the Bark scale.
note: Bark scale: „skala Bark” (Polish Wikipedia: „Bark (skala)”), unit „bark”.

definition: A value drawn over time along the waveform.
A small picture of a whole sound used to find one's way in it.
note: Bare „podgląd” means preview, so it is avoided as the main term.

definition: The overview of one sound as Playhead draws it: waveform, curves and marks in one band.
note: „Pasek” is the natural Polish UI word for a horizontal band; it is also used for toolbars („pasek narzędzi”), but „pasek dźwięku” is unambiguous in context. „Taśma” is evocative (tape) but suggests a recording medium; „pas” is neutral but stiff. A lane is „tor”, part of a „pasek”.

definition: A named way to draw a strip, written as a short code of layers.
note: „Wygląd” is the literal choice, but Polish UIs use „Wygląd” for Appearance/theme settings (and „motyw” for theme), which the source says to keep apart. „Styl” reads well („kod stylu”, „Styl: …”). „Odsłona” is idiomatic („w nowej odsłonie”) but also means a page view.

definition: The short text that defines a look, for example "form:overlay,shape:mirror,lane:harshness".
note: Follows the choice made for look. The code keywords stay in English.

definition: One element of a look: a waveform, spectrogram, curve, set of marks or sections.
note: „Warstwa” is universal in Polish graphics and audio software. Like the English, it is also used for the separated sound layers in the layer remix tool; „element” is the fallback if the two meanings must be kept apart.

definition: A horizontal band of a strip that holds one curve.
note: As in „tor automatyki”. This avoids „ścieżka” (track) and „pasmo” (frequency band).

definition: Curves drawn in one shared band instead of separate lanes.
note: Adjective (krzywe nałożone); noun „nałożenie”. Distinct from mirrored („lustrzane”).

definition: Drawn symmetrically above and below a centre line, like a waveform.
note: Adjective that agrees with its noun (krzywa lustrzana, przebieg lustrzany). Not „nałożone” (overlaid).

definition: Drawn upwards from the bottom of the band.
note: Adverbial option label, alongside „lustrzane” and „nałożone”.

definition: A compact chart that folds a curve into coloured bands of increasing intensity.
note: I found no competing Polish term; the calque is transparent. Give „(horizon chart)” on first mention in docs.

definition: A waveform whose height follows a curve, for example perceived loudness, instead of the peak level.
note: „Rzeźbić brzmienie” is a common Polish studio metaphor, so the literal rendering works; the adjective follows the noun, as in classifying Polish terms (przebieg szczytowy). „Kształtowany” is plainer but less distinctive.
alternatives: przebieg kształtowany; rzeźbiona fala; sculpted waveform

definition: The ordinary peak waveform drawn as a thin line behind another layer.
Ticks along the strip at events, onsets, beats or section boundaries.
note: Ardour and Audacity pl: „znacznik” = marker.

definition: The text that says what each colour and line of a strip shows.
How much Playhead analyses: fast (curves only), sound effect, or music.
A number or curve computed from a sound that describes one of its properties.
note: Polish MPEG-7 and MIR literature: „deskryptory audio”.

definition: A descriptor used as input to a classifier or search.
note: Polish machine-learning usage („wektor cech”, „ekstrakcja cech”).

definition: How much is happening: spectral change and the density of events.
note: Literal and clear. „Ruchliwość” is more idiomatic for a busy sound but sounds more evaluative; „zagęszczenie zdarzeń” covers only half the definition.

definition: How exciting or calming a sound is, after the psychological dimension of the same name.
note: Polish emotion psychology: „pobudzenie” (the valence–arousal model is „walencja–pobudzenie”).

definition: How unpleasant a sound is to listen to, computed from psychoacoustic annoyance; not the same as roughness.
note: Studio Polish calls harsh sound „ostry”, but „ostrość” is taken by sharpness and „chropowatość”/„szorstkość” by roughness, so a third word is needed. „Nieprzyjemność” follows the definition directly; „przykrość” is shorter but sounds emotional (sorrow); „jazgotliwość” is vivid but colloquial and suggests loud din.

definition: Build-up and release over time, after the model of musical tension by Farbood (2012).
note: Polish music theory pair „napięcie – rozładowanie (odprężenie)”.

definition: How far the harmony is from rest, from the tonal interval space.
How much a moment differs from what came before.
note: Foote's novelty function is „funkcja nowości”. Keep it distinct from „zaskoczenie widmowe” and „informacja własna”.

definition: Change of the spectrum that loudness does not explain.
note: Literal and natural. It only works if surprisal is „informacja własna” and never bare „zaskoczenie”. „Niespodzianka” sounds playful; the descriptive form is clear but long.
alternatives: niespodzianka widmowa; nieoczekiwana zmiana widma; spectral surprise

definition: Information content of an event: the less expected, the higher.
note: Polish information-theory term for self-information (Polish Wikipedia: „Ilość informacji”). Music-cognition papers sometimes write „zaskoczenie”; that is avoided here to keep it apart from spectral surprise.

definition: Where a piece moves to a new part, signed: up where sound enters, down where it falls away or breaks off.
note: „Strukturalna” matches MIR usage („analiza struktury utworu”); „zmiana formy” is the musicological wording. In the app's short legends, up/down are „wejście” / „spadek lub urwanie”.
alternatives: zmiana formy; przejście formalne; structural change

definition: How clearly a regular pulse is felt at each moment.
note: Grosche & Müller's PLP = „dominujący puls lokalny”. Avoid „siła beatu/miary” (beat strength). Its measure is „wyrazistość pulsu” (pulse clarity).

definition: The moment a sound or note begins.
note: Ardour pl („Rozdziel na początkach dźwięków perkusyjnych”, „czas między początkami dźwięków”); MIR jargon „onset”. It is a moment; „atak” is the phase and „transjent” the change.

definition: How strongly new sound arrives at each moment; peaks are hits.
note: Technical docs may use „funkcja detekcji początków” (onset detection function).

definition: One distinct sound within a file, such as a hit, a step or a creak, with a start and an end.
note: As in „detekcja zdarzeń dźwiękowych” (sound event detection).

definition: The first part of a sound, from its start to its peak.
note: Studio and musical-acoustics usage. LMMS and Audacity pl use „narastanie” for the ADSR stage.

definition: The sustained, often tonal, part of a sound after its attack.
note: „Dodać ciała” is a common studio idiom, but „ciało” as the name of a part reads oddly. „Korpus” works in „atak i korpus”. Acoustics textbooks say „stan ustalony”.

definition: The part of a sound in which it dies away.
note: This is not the ADSR decay stage (LMMS and Audacity pl: „opadanie”). „Wybrzmiewanie” is a good synonym but is used for the ring time tool.

definition: The late part of a decay, including reverberation.
note: Studio usage („ogon pogłosu”).

definition: A short, fast change of level and spectrum, typically at an attack.
note: Polish Wikipedia („Transjent”) and Ardour pl; acoustics textbooks use „stan nieustalony”.

definition: The regular pulse a listener taps along to.
note: Polish music theory (miary w takcie; Audacity pl „Miary i takty”). Ardour and LMMS pl use „uderzenie”, which is avoided here because „uderzenie” means a hit (event). „Beat” is common in speech; note that „bit” means a hip-hop instrumental.

definition: The first beat of a bar.
note: Musicians say „raz” („wejście na raz”). „Mocna część taktu” is broader.

definition: A group of beats, usually four.
note: The US „measure” is also „takt”.

definition: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).
note: „Uderzeń na minutę” is the fixed Polish reading of BPM (Audacity pl). It is the one place where „uderzenie” refers to the beat.

definition: A part of a piece, such as an intro or chorus, found from where its sound changes.
note: Producers say „sekcja”. Musicologists say „część” or „odcinek”, but „część” is too generic for a UI label and also means a movement.

definition: How much a sound returns to states it has been in before.
note: As in recurrence plots („wykresy rekurencyjne”) and RQA („ilościowa analiza rekurencji”) in Polish nonlinear-dynamics writing.

definition: How often a pattern repeats, in Hz.
note: As in „częstotliwość powtarzania impulsów” (pulse repetition frequency).

definition: How strongly a sound is periodic (pitched) rather than noisy.
How steadily a sound's phases advance; 1 for a steady tone, near 0 for noise.
How much a sound changes when played backwards; high for hits that decay.
note: „Strzałka czasu” is the established Polish physics term for the arrow of time (Polish Wikipedia), so the metaphor carries over. „Nieodwracalność czasowa” is the technical term, for docs only.
alternatives: kierunkowość czasu; nieodwracalność czasowa; time arrow

definition: How much a sound consists of clicks, cracks and crackle, from spectral kurtosis.
note: Polish acousticians use „impulsowość” for impulsive noise (M. Gałuszka, twojazielonka.org; „hałas impulsowy”). „Impulsywność” is the everyday word for temperament; „trzaskliwość” is vivid but unusual. Avoid „kolczastość” (spikiness).

definition: A statistic that is 0 for steady noise, −1 for a steady tone and large for clicks.
How fast the spectrum's centre moves up or down, in octaves per second.
note: Literal and short. The descriptive „prędkość środka widma” is exact but long.
alternatives: ruch widmowy; prędkość środka widma; spectral motion

definition: The centre of mass of a spectrum; a measure of brightness.
note: Polish MIR and MPEG-7 writing uses both „centroid” and „środek ciężkości widma”.

definition: Spectral change that does not move the centre, as when a spectrum spreads or narrows.
note: „Przekształcanie” is the closest literal match but collides with „przekształcenie” (a transform, e.g. „przekształcenie Fouriera”). „Deformacja” sounds like damage.

definition: Whether events come regularly (below 0), at random (0) or in bursts (above 0).
note: No established Polish term: Polish complex-systems papers usually keep „burstiness”. „Seryjność” (from „seria”, a burst as in „seria strzałów”) is my proposal; it can also suggest „produkcja seryjna”, so the loan is safer in docs.

definition: How evenly a sound's energy is spread over time.
The time a sound takes to fall by 60 dB.
note: „Czas pogłosu” (T60) is the room-acoustics term (PN-EN ISO 3382); for a single sound „czas zaniku” is clearer. „Czas wybrzmiewania” is used for the ring time tool.

definition: How quickly a vibrating body loses energy.
note: Physics: „tłumienie drgań”; LMMS pl „Tłumienie”.

definition: What an impacted object is made of, as heard: damped, glass-like or metal-like.
One frequency component of a sound.
note: Polish musical acoustics („tony składowe”). „Parcjał” is additive-synthesis jargon. Bare „składowa” is avoided as the term because of „składowa stała” (DC offset).

definition: A partial above the lowest one.
note: Audacity pl: „alikwoty”. Polish usage often treats „alikwot” as a harmonic only; here it includes inharmonic partials.

definition: With partials that are not whole-number multiples of a fundamental, as in bells and struck metal.
Automatic checks for clipping, DC offset, silence and cut tails.
A test that edits a sound in a known way and checks that the analysis changes as it must.
note: „Autotest” is the familiar Polish IT word for a built-in self-test; „samosprawdzenie” is literal but clumsy. It must not be „test jednostkowy” (unit test); the technical name for docs is „test metamorficzny”.

definition: A tool that turns down resonances only while the sound is harsh.
note: Imperative, per the command convention; noun form „łagodzenie brzmienia” for headings. „Złagodzić” is what Polish engineers say about taming harsh resonances. The literal „redukuj nieprzyjemność” ties the tool to the curve name. The loan works by analogy with „de-esser”, which Polish keeps in English. This is not a de-esser (a de-esser keys on level in one band).

definition: A tool that splits a sound into its transient part and its sustained part, to rebalance them.
note: Noun title, as in English. „Atak i ciało” is idiomatic studio speech but reads oddly as a title; „podtrzymanie” recalls ADSR sustain. Do not call it „kształtowanie transjentów” (a transient shaper works on level, not on a split).
alternatives: atak i ciało; atak i podtrzymanie; attack & body

definition: A tool that separates a sound into layers and mixes them again at new levels.
note: „Remiks” is naturalised Polish and short; „przemiksowanie warstw” is the plain verbal noun; „rozkład na warstwy” names only the first step.
alternatives: przemiksowanie warstw; rozkład na warstwy; layer remix

definition: A tool that turns the tension curve into gain and brightness automation.
note: Polish names such processors after the process („kształtowanie transjentów” for transient shaper). „Kształtownik” is the literal agent noun but in Polish it means a steel section; „modelator” is acceptable but rare.
alternatives: modelator napięcia; kształtownik napięcia; tension shaper

definition: A tool that finds and crossfades loop points where the sound repeats best.
note: „Kreator” is the Polish UI word for a wizard, which fits a tool that finds the points for you. „Zapętlacz” is playful and idiomatic. „Generator” clashes with the Workbench generator.

definition: Several slightly different versions of one sound, to avoid repetition in games.
note: „Wariacje” suggests musical variations; game-audio usage is „warianty”.

definition: A tool that repairs what the quality checks flag before a sound is exported.
note: The vocabulary term is a noun, but Playhead names the tool with a verb („Clean up for export”), so the app uses the imperative „Wyczyść przed eksportem”, following the command convention.
alternatives: wyczyść przed eksportem; porządki przed eksportem; przygotowanie do eksportu

definition: Reverberation fed only from the decays of the events, keeping the attacks dry.
note: Literal and clear in studio Polish („ogon”, „suchy”). „Wybrzmienia” is more elegant but less exact. The half-loan is how engineers would say it aloud.
alternatives: pogłos wybrzmień; pogłos tylko na ogonach; reverb na ogonach

definition: Saturation applied only to the events' attacks or bodies.
note: Imperative; noun form „nasycanie uderzeń” or „saturacja uderzeń”. „Nasycić” maps directly to saturation („nasycenie”). „Podkręcić” (crank up) is idiomatic but sounds like a level boost. „Przesterować” is the natural word for drive but points to clipping („przesterowanie”).
alternatives: podkręć uderzenia; przesteruj uderzenia; drive na uderzeniach

definition: A tool that lengthens or shortens how long each event rings after its peak.
note: „Wybrzmiewać” means exactly „to ring out”. „Dzwonienie” is literal but evokes phones and bells. The measured decay time stays „czas zaniku (T60)”.
alternatives: długość wybrzmienia; czas dzwonienia; ring time

definition: A tool that evens out how loud the events are, one gain per event, without touching their shape.
note: Imperative; noun form „wyrównywanie głośności zdarzeń”. The bare „wyrównaj zdarzenia” is closer to the English but can be read as „align the events” in time. Do not call it „kompresja” (a compressor changes the shape).
alternatives: wyrównaj zdarzenia; wyrównywanie głośności zdarzeń; level events

definition: Turn stereo into mono with the channels' phase lined up, so nothing cancels.
note: Imperative; noun form „składanie do mono”. „Złożyć” keeps the folding metaphor and stays distinct from the plain sum („zsumuj do mono”; Audacity pl „Miksuj stereo do mono”). The descriptive form is exact but long.
alternatives: zmiksuj do mono z wyrównaniem fazy; mono bez wygaszania; fold to mono

definition: Make or widen stereo only after the attacks, keeping attacks centred and the result mono-compatible.
note: Imperative; noun form „poszerzanie ogonów”. It pairs with „pogłos na ogonach”. „Wybrzmienia” is softer but less precise about what is widened.
alternatives: poszerz wybrzmienia; stereo na ogonach; widen tails

definition: Turn more channels into fewer.
note: Broadcast and post-production usage keeps the loan („downmix 5.1 do stereo”); „downmiks” is the Polonised spelling.
alternatives: downmiks; zgranie do mniejszej liczby kanałów

definition: How well a stereo sound survives being summed to mono.
note: TVP technical requirements: „kompatybilność sygnału stereofonicznego z monofonicznym”.

definition: Making two signals less alike while keeping their spectrum, to widen a stereo image.
Regular notches in a spectrum when a signal is summed with a delayed copy of itself.
note: Polish Wikipedia: „Filtr grzebieniowy”.

definition: Loss of level when signals of opposite phase are summed.
note: Studio speech also says „sygnały się znoszą”; physics: „interferencja destrukcyjna”.

definition: A faint smear of a sound before its attack, caused by frame-based processing.
note: Polish perceptual-coding texts mostly keep „pre-echo” („zjawisko pre-echa”); the Polish calques exist but are rare.

definition: An equaliser: a filter that changes the level of frequency bands.
note: Polish Wikipedia: „Korektor (akustyka)”; Audacity pl: „korektor graficzny”. Controls show „EQ”.

definition: An EQ whose band gains follow the level in each band.
Parameter changes over time, recorded or drawn.
note: Ardour pl and LMMS pl („ścieżka automatyki”, „edytor automatyki”).

definition: A processor that turns loud passages down by a ratio above a threshold.
note: Polish Wikipedia: „Kompresor dynamiki”; Audacity and LMMS pl.

definition: The level above which a processor acts.
note: Audacity, Ardour, LMMS pl.

definition: How strongly a compressor turns the level down above its threshold.
note: Audacity pl („Współczynnik kompresji”), LMMS pl („Współczynnik”). Hardware controls often keep „Ratio”.

definition: How fast a processor reacts when the level rises.
note: Studio usage. Audacity and LMMS pl use „czas narastania”.

definition: How fast a processor recovers when the level falls.
note: Studio Polish varies: „powrót”, „zwolnienie”, often plain „release”. Audacity pl has „czas opadania”; LMMS pl has „czas zanikania”, which is avoided because „zanikanie” = decay here.

definition: A processor or condition that opens only above a threshold.
note: Audacity pl („Bramka szumów”), LMMS pl. BS.1770 gating = „bramkowanie”.

definition: Soft distortion that adds harmonics and rounds peaks.
note: Studio usage prefers „saturacja”; „nasycenie” is the native word (nasycenie taśmy, lampy).

definition: Audible rise and fall of the background caused by a compressor.
How alike the events are in loudness.
Effects applied one after another to a sound.
A saved set of settings.
note: Ardour, LMMS and Audacity pl all use „preset” (presety, presetu).

definition: A gradual blend from one sound into another.
Combining the spectrum of one sound with the envelope or excitation of another.
Filtering one sound by another, for example by a room's impulse response.
note: Mathematical term (Polish Wikipedia: „Splot (analiza matematyczna)”); studio speech uses „pogłos splotowy” and the calque „konwolucja”.

definition: Giving one sound the level envelope of another.
note: „Obwiednia” as in Audacity pl and Polish Wikipedia („Obwiednia dźwięku”).

definition: Multiplying two signals, which creates sum and difference frequencies.
note: LMMS pl.

definition: Built from many short grains of sound.
note: Polish Wikipedia: „Synteza granularna”; grain = „ziarno”.

definition: A short added sound placed at a moment of another sound to emphasise it.
note: „Akcent” is natural (accent = emphasis) but a musician may read it as a louder note. „Podkreślenie” is plainer. Film post calls such layers „sweetener”.

definition: A part of the app that makes new sounds from parameters.
A sound generator built from oscillators, noise, envelopes and filters.
A physical model of a struck object of a given material and shape.
note: Use „Uderzenie” as the generator title and „model uderzenia” in docs, to keep it apart from hits (uderzenia = events). Game-audio slang: „impakt”.

definition: Rebuilding a sound from parameters measured on it, such as its partials and decays.
Made of resonant modes, each with a frequency and a decay.
note: As in „synteza modalna”; mechanics says „mody drgań” or „postaci drgań własnych”.

definition: A continuous sound made of many small events, such as rain, fire or gravel.
A generator in which an action, such as an object moving or a force, drives the sound of a medium that responds to it (gravel, water, air).
note: „Zasada akcji i reakcji” is the everyday Polish name of Newton's third law, so the pair is instantly understood. „Działanie” is more formal; „odpowiedź” sounds like signal processing.
alternatives: działanie i reakcja; działanie i odpowiedź; action & reaction

definition: What reacts to an action: gravel, leaves, water, air, sparks or a force field.
note: Physics term for a propagation medium; „medium” is also understood.

definition: A curve that controls a sound's parameters over time.
note: „Sterować” is the Polish verb for driving a parameter. „Napędowa” is mechanically literal. „Wysterowanie” in Polish audio means drive or level, so it would suggest gain only.
alternatives: krzywa napędowa; krzywa wysterowania; drive curve

definition: How slowly a reaction settles after the action stops.
Everyday sounds performed and recorded in sync with picture.
note: Polish film-sound terminology: „efekty synchroniczne”, „imitacja synchroniczna”, with the artist called „imitator” (Polish film-sound article on ejournals.eu; noiz.ai pl „Kinowe efekty synchroniczne (Foley)”). „Foley” is understood in game audio.

definition: The background sound of a place.
note: Polish film post-production calls these tracks „atmosfery” (ejournals.eu article: „atmosfery, efekty boczne, synchroniczne”); general texts say „tło dźwiękowe”.

definition: A short sound played once, such as a hit or a UI click.
note: Sampler and game-audio loan.

definition: The sound of something moving fast past the listener.
note: Sound designers use the loan; „świst” is the Polish word in general texts (noiz.ai pl: „charakterystyczne świsty”).

definition: The last steps before export: format, channels, fades and level.

note: „Tektura” is the material; „karton” is also used colloquially and means a carton.

definition: A long solid body, such as a rod or beam.
note: Not „takt” (musical bar).

definition: A thin flat body.
A stretched skin, as on a drum.
A thin curved body, such as a can or pot.
note: Mechanics term („teoria powłok”).

definition: A stiff string or wire that rings with slightly stretched (inharmonic) partials.
note: Polish names a vibrating stretched element „struna” (piano strings are steel wire); „drut” is the material. In Workbench the impact-model shape „Wire / string” is „Drut / struna”.

definition: A hollow body with flat sides.
note: As in „pudło rezonansowe”.

definition: A row of a DAW session that holds clips on the timeline and has its own mixer channel.
note: Ardour, Audacity and LMMS pl 'ścieżka'. Not 'tor' (a band inside a strip) or 'kanał' (one signal of a sound file).

definition: A track that holds other tracks: it sums their sound and can show them as one.
note: REAPER and Cubase say 'folder track'; Polish users say 'folder'. Playhead: 'Ścieżki w folderze'.

definition: One piece of audio or MIDI on a track, placed at a point in time.
note: Here 'zdarzenie' is a sound event and 'region' a named span of time (Ardour pl and Logic call clips regions).

definition: All of one piece of DAW work: its tracks, clips, routing and settings; also called a project.
note: Polish users say 'projekt'; Ardour pl 'sesja'.

definition: The time axis of a session, along which clips are placed.
A named point in time stored in a session or a sound file (a cue in a WAV file).
note: Studio loan. Not 'znacznik': 'znaczniki' are the marks Playhead draws on a strip.

definition: A named span of time with a start and an end, stored in a session or a sound file.
note: REAPER usage. Ardour pl and Logic call clips 'regiony'; here a region is a span of time.

definition: Making a clip or an edit jump to the nearest grid line, marker, clip edge or onset while it is moved.
note: Playhead: 'Przyciągaj do początków'.

definition: Silencing a track without removing it; the button is often labelled M.
note: Buttons 'Wycisz' or M.

definition: Hearing only the soloed tracks; the button is often labelled S.
The level control of a mixer channel.
note: Studio speech 'suwak' or 'fader'.

definition: Where a sound sits between left and right; also the control that sets it.
note: Studio term (panorama, f.; panoramowanie in LMMS pl). 'Pan' is heard as a knob label only.

definition: A mixer channel that sums the signals sent to it, so they can be processed together (a drum bus, a reverb bus).
note: Ardour pl 'szyna'; studio speech also 'bus'.

definition: The bus everything is summed into before the output: what is rendered as the mix.
A copy of a track's signal sent to a bus at its own level, while the track keeps playing.
An effect in a channel's own signal path, which all of the signal passes through.
note: Studio loan.

definition: How signals travel between tracks, buses, sends and outputs.
The sum of all tracks as it is heard; also the work of balancing them.
note: Playhead: 'miks folderu'.

definition: A submix of related tracks (drums, dialogue, music) rendered to its own file, so the parts can be mixed or delivered separately.
note: Loan used in post-production and game audio (pl. stemy).

definition: A point where the waveform crosses zero; cuts and loop points made there do not click.
note: Standard signal-processing term.

definition: The distance in dB between the highest level a signal reaches and the level where it would clip.
note: Studio usage; 'headroom' loan also heard (Playhead: 'brak zapasu').

definition: The span in dB between a sound's loud and quiet parts, or between the highest level a system takes and its noise floor.
note: A level measure in dB; the loudness range (zakres głośności, LRA) is a loudness measure in LU.

definition: How much the loudness of a programme varies, in LU: the span between the 10th and 95th percentile of its short-term loudness.
note: EBU Tech 3342; Ardour pl 'Zakres głośności'.

definition: The loudness of a whole programme, with silence and quiet passages gated out, in LUFS.
note: EBU R 128.

definition: Loudness over a sliding 3 s window, in LUFS.
note: EBU Tech 3341.

definition: Loudness over a sliding 400 ms window, in LUFS.
note: EBU Tech 3341.

definition: The integrated loudness a programme is delivered or played at, such as −23 LUFS for EBU R 128 broadcast or about −14 LUFS on streaming services.
Bringing two versions to the same loudness before comparing them, so that the louder one does not seem better only because it is louder.
note: As in Playhead ('Dopasuj głośność'); level the events is a different tool.

definition: Switching between two versions, ideally at matched loudness, to hear which is better.
A finished recording played for comparison while mixing or mastering.
The ratio of peak to RMS level, in dB: high for punchy, dynamic sound, low for dense, compressed sound.
The root mean square of a signal over a window: its average power, as a level.
How different the two channels are, from mono (not at all) to wide.
note: Plain 'szerokość' on controls (LMMS pl). Matches widen the tails = poszerz ogony.

definition: How a quantity, usually level, changes over the course of a sound; also a drawn curve that controls a parameter.
note: Standard (obwiednia, f.): Audacity pl 'Obwiednia', LMMS pl. Level envelope = obwiednia poziomu (envelope transfer).

definition: A range of frequencies measured or processed together: an EQ band, a critical band, a mel band.
A filter that passes the frequencies above its cutoff and attenuates those below.
note: Standard Polish electronics term.

definition: A filter that passes the frequencies below its cutoff and attenuates those above.
note: Standard Polish electronics term.

definition: A compressor with a very high ratio and a fast attack that keeps the level below a ceiling.
A compressor that works on several frequency bands separately.
A processor that raises or lowers the attack and the sustain of sounds independently of their level.
note: Transient = transjent in this vocabulary.

definition: A second input through which another signal controls a processor, as when music is turned down under dialogue.
Turning one sound down automatically while another plays, usually with a sidechained compressor.
The dense reflections of a sound in a space, or an effect that imitates them.
note: As in reverb on the tails = pogłos na ogonach.

definition: An effect that plays the sound again after a set time, often repeating and fading (echo).
Low-level noise added when the bit depth is reduced, so that the rounding error becomes noise instead of distortion.
The last stage before release: the final EQ, dynamics and loudness of a mix, and checks for the delivery format.
The moment in a dance track when the full beat and bass come in, usually after a build-up or a breakdown.
note: Playhead never uses 'drop' for a fall in level.

definition: A passage that raises tension towards a drop: rising pitch, filter sweeps, faster rolls, a riser.
A passage where the beat and bass fall away, leaving pads, chords or vocals.
note: Not 'wyciszenie' (= mute).

definition: A sound that rises in pitch, brightness or level to lead into a drop or a transition.
note: Producer loan (pl. risery); no Polish word in use.

definition: A glide through a range of frequencies: a tone or noise whose pitch or brightness moves, or a filter swept across the spectrum.
note: Native word for a pitch or brightness glide (ślizg, m.); studio speech also says 'sweep'.

definition: A stored position in a track that a DJ or a player jumps to or starts from.
The beats and bars of a track as a grid, used to sync, loop and jump in time.
note: Beat = miara in this vocabulary; Playhead: 'siatka miar'. DJ software keeps 'beatgrid'.

definition: Bringing two tracks to the same tempo with their beats aligned.
A run of bars, usually 8, 16 or 32 in dance music, that forms one musical unit; DJs mix at phrase boundaries.
The tonal centre and scale of a piece, such as A minor; DJs mix tracks in compatible keys (harmonic mixing).
